answer: No. Your records show you did not have a blood clot in your lung. On 8 July 2025 you had a CT scan of the chest with contrast (a CT angiogram, which looks for clots in the lung arteries). It was done because of chest wall pain, and your D-dimer blood test that day was raised at 0.92 (normal is 0.49 or less). A raised D-dimer is common and not specific, so it prompted the scan. The scan report says there was no pulmonary embolism and your lungs were clear. Your record lists pulmonary embolism as 'ruled out'. The chest wall pain was marked resolved by 22 July 2025. The scan did mention mild wear-and-tear changes in the spine of your upper back, which is common and usually not a worry.
short: A chest CT angiogram on 2025-07-08 showed no pulmonary embolism; the diagnosis is recorded as ruled out. The raised D-dimer that day prompted the scan, and the chest wall pain resolved by 2025-07-22.
